{{Short description|Australian statistician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2019}}
'''Eugene B. Seneta''' (born 1941) is Professor Emeritus, School of Mathematics and Statistics, [[University of Sydney]], known for his work in probability and [[nonnegative matrix|non-negative matrices]],<ref>{{Cite book|author=E. Seneta|title=Non-negative matrices and Markov chains|series=Springer Series in Statistics No. 21|publisher=Springer|location=U.S.A.|year=2006|pages=287|ISBN=0-387-29765-0|mr=2209438}}</ref> applications and history.<ref>{{Cite book|author=[[Chris Heyde|C. C. Heyde]] and E. Seneta|title=Statisticians of the Centuries|publisher=Springer-Verlag|location=New York|year=2001|pages=500|ISBN=0-387-95329-9}}</ref> He is known for the [[variance gamma process|variance gamma model]] in financial mathematics (the [[variance gamma process]]).<ref>Madan and Seneta 1990; Seneta 2004.</ref> He was Professor, School of Mathematics and Statistics at the University of Sydney from 1979 until retirement, and an Elected Fellow since 1985 of the [[Australian Academy of Science]].<ref>[http://www.science.org.au/fellows/fellowship-list.html Fellows of the Australian Academy of Science] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111006230332/http://science.org.au/fellows/fellowship-list.html |date=2011-10-06 }}</ref> In 2007 Seneta was awarded the [[Hannan Medal]] in Statistical Science<ref>[http://www.science.org.au/awards/awardees/2007awards.html Australian Academy of Science 2007 Awardees] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100427071057/http://www.science.org.au/awards/awardees/2007awards.html |date=2010-04-27 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web
|url= http://www.statsoc.org.au/objectlibrary/278?filename=SSAI%20119%20web.pdf
|title= Eugene Seneta Receives the Hannan Medal in 2007: Newsletter, Statistical Society of Australia, Incorporated
|author= Chris Heyde
|year= 2007
|access-date= 19 February 2011
|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110216101830/http://www.statsoc.org.au/objectlibrary/278?filename=SSAI%20119%20web.pdf
|archive-date= 16 February 2011
|url-status= dead
}} page 3.</ref> 
by the Australian Academy of Science, for his seminal work in probability and statistics; for his work connected with [[branching process]]es, history of probability and statistics, and many other areas.

==References==
{{Reflist}}

* E. Seneta (2004). Fitting the variance-gamma model to financial data, Stochastic methods and their applications, ''J. Appl. Probab.'' 41A, 177–187.
* E. Seneta (2001). Characterization by orthogonal polynomial systems of finite Markov chains, ''J. Appl. Probab.'', 38A, 42–52.
*Madan D, Seneta E. (1990). The variance gamma (v.g.) model for share market returns, ''Journal of Business'', 63 (1990), 511–524.
* [[Peter Gavin Hall|P. Hall]] and E. Seneta (1988). Products of independent normally attracted random variables, ''Probability Theory and Related Fields'', 78, 135–142.
* E. Seneta (1974). Regularly varying functions in the theory of simple branching processes, ''Advances in Applied Probability'', 6, 408–420.
* E. Seneta (1973). The simple branching process with infinite mean, I, ''Journal of Applied Probability'', 10, 206–212.
* E. Seneta (1973). A Tauberian theorem of R. Landau and W. Feller, ''The Annals of Probability'', 1, 1057–1058.
